transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Diego (Redwood CSM), Maya (HelioGen Infra Lead), Tomas (CTO), Sofia (NetEng)
---
[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. we'll do the usual 30 min ops + 30 min tuning if we need it, but feel free to flag interruptions. quick roll call?
[00:09] Maya Chen: maya here, i'm with sofia and tomas. we saw a couple of tail spikes this week after the midnight deploys.
[00:15] Tomás Alvarez: hi all. quick context, spikes mostly around long-seq chat requests hitting ~95th to 99th. cost is fine for now but latency variability is blocking ux.
[00:25] Priya Raman: ok noted. is this across dedicated nodes or the canary private deployment?
[00:30] Sofia Rinaldi: it was on the private pilot in our VPC, on the canary pool. not seen on hosted.
[00:38] Priya Raman: makes sense — we saw a similar signature to an earlier KV-cache miss pattern. sometimes prefix cache eviction + low MTU path causes additional RTTs.
[00:47] Jordan Park: quick agenda: 1) incident recap and logs, 2) kernel upgrade plan (low-risk), 3) networking checks (MTU/traceroutes), 4) plan for 1k RPS run. sound good?
[00:56] Tomás Alvarez: yes. can we prioritize the rollback path — last time rollback was convolved with k8s draining, which added extra windows of throttling.
[01:05] Priya Raman: absolutely. our patch includes an automated rollback flag — can revert in under 3 minutes, and we documented a safe drain sequence. i'll send the runbook.
[01:12] Maya Chen: last time the host kernel bump changed NIC offload behavior and we saw odd retransmits. any notes on that?
[01:20] Priya Raman: good catch. the kernel patch toggles a NIC offload knob on certain drivers to reduce copy overhead; we can disable that in staging to validate. i'll include the exact sysctl and ethtool commands.
[01:28] Sofia Rinaldi: we'll need those before we run anything on canary. also, please include the rollback aws route53 TTL impacts — we had some DNS caching after failback.
[01:36] Jordan Park: noted. Diego — can you take point on security docs?
[01:40] Diego Morales: yep, i'll bundle SOC2 scope, KMS integration notes (we have HSM options), and the redacted audit trail example. will post link to the shared drive.
[01:48] Tomás Alvarez: are there any open compliance blockers for Private in prod? we have auditors asking about data residency and key control.
[01:55] Diego Morales: Publicly, Private supports customer-managed KMS and we can offer HSM-backed keys for the enterprise package. i'll confirm the required attestation text for auditors.
[02:03] Jordan Park: switching to network findings — sofia, you mentioned you captured traceroutes?
[02:08] Sofia Rinaldi: yes, we ran traceroutes to the canary node, and one path went through an intermediary with MTU 1400, causing fragmentation. suspect the path MTU plus an unexpected link caused 2x RTT for some requests.
[02:18] Priya Raman: that fragmentation would definitely blow up tail latency for longer tokens, because of extra retransmits and extra time in the GPU queue. we'll add MTU detection to the agent and emit a warning metric.
[02:27] Maya Chen: is that something we can flip provisionally in the routing policy? like prefer alternate region or fallback node with compatible MTU?
[02:33] Priya Raman: yes we have smart-routing policy that can prefer a model variant in the same region with a different path. currently routing is based on latency and capacity; we can add an MTU health probe as a tiebreaker.
[02:42] Jordan Park: good idea. would that affect cost? switching to a different variant can change per-token CPU/GPU usage.
[02:48] Tomás Alvarez: cost is secondary to UX for now, but call it out so we can estimate.
[02:53] Priya Raman: noted, we'll include delta estimates.
[03:00] Jordan Park: on observability — Diego, we asked for prefix KV logging. do we have a plan to enable it without spamming the logs?
[03:06] Diego Morales: yes, we'll turn on sampling (1%) and a short 48-hour window on the canary. that should flag whether eviction patterns correlate to the latency spikes.
[03:14] Sofia Rinaldi: can you correlate those logs to request ids? that helps us map from app traces to infra events.
[03:20] Priya Raman: we emit a request_id on entry; we'll surface that in the KV log entries. i'll confirm the mapping schema.
[03:27] Tomás Alvarez: great. now the benchmark — what's the plan for the 1k RPS run?
[03:31] Priya Raman: propose a 30-minute steady-state at 1k RPS, with a 10-min warmup and 10-min cool-down. collect p50/p95/p99, also track queue depths and GPU utilisation.
[03:40] Maya Chen: can we do an incremental ramp instead? we want to observe breakpoints.
[03:44] Priya Raman: yes, we can run a staircase: 200, 400, 700, 1k with 5-10 minutes per step.
[03:49] Jordan Park: we'll schedule that for next week, tentatively 2027-12-16. HelioGen to confirm their blackout window.
[03:55] Sofia Rinaldi: we have a maintenance window that day from 02:00–04:00 local; avoid that.
[04:00] Jordan Park: ok noted, we'll avoid the window.
[04:05] Tomás Alvarez: about model quantization — we briefly discussed switching to int8 to save compute; any risks to quality?
[04:13] Priya Raman: quant profiles are model dependent. int8 can reduce cost but may increase perplexity on certain prompts. Redwood Optimize suggests candidate quant profile per workload; we'll run a small A/B against our eval prompts.
[04:24] Maya Chen: can we run that in parallel with the staging kernel upgrade or will that confound results?
[04:29] Priya Raman: keep them separate — kernel changes can affect latency independently. we'll sequence: 1) kernel patch + rollback validation, 2) find baseline, 3) quant A/B.
[04:36] Diego Morales: i'll add separate tracking tags in the metrics so we can gate the analyses.
[04:40] Jordan Park: any blockers on running the kernel patch in staging this week?
[04:44] Priya Raman: none from Redwood side. we just need canary access and permission to run for a 1-hour window.
[04:49] Sofia Rinaldi: we'll provision a 2-hour slot to be safe and provide a pre-flight checklist to the Redwood team.
[04:55] Jordan Park: excellent. quick note: last week's incident logs included a misspelling of model name in the telemetry ("Red wood-b200"), so cross-check model tags in the telemetry pipeline.
[05:03] Priya Raman: ha, yes those OCR-ish transcriptions; we'll patch the tagging.
[05:08] Maya Chen: on security — Diego, when can we expect the SOC2 artefacts? auditors asked for recent evidence.
[05:13] Diego Morales: i'll upload the scope doc and sample encrypted logs by 2027-12-09; for full attestations we might need a brief NDA addendum. i'll follow up.
[05:20] Tomás Alvarez: ok. also, about data residency, we want proof that logs don't exit region — can Redwood provide a log flow diagram?
[05:26] Diego Morales: yes, i'll include a regional data flow diagram and mark the control plane endpoints.
[05:31] Jordan Park: jumping to recap — agreed actions: Priya pushes kernel patch to staging with rollback; Diego sends security pack; Sofia runs traceroutes and confirms MTU; HelioGen to run a short latency spike test. anyone add?
[05:42] Maya Chen: add: enable prefix KV sampling on canary for 48 hours.
[05:47] Jordan Park: done. next meeting — same time next week?
[05:50] Tomás Alvarez: yes works for us.
[05:52] Jordan Park: ok i'll recap and email the runbook + links. thanks everyone.
[05:56] Sofia Rinaldi: thanks.
[05:57] Priya Raman: thanks all.
---

Recorded notes (quick):
- Root cause hypothesis: path MTU fragmentation + occasional KV prefix eviction producing extra backend RTTs, exacerbated by NIC offload change in kernel patch.
- Mitigation path: kernel patch in staging with offload knob disabled for validation; prefix KV logging at sample rate; MTU detection probe in agent + routing tiebreaker.
- Success criteria for benchmark: p99 improvement or stability within SLA band (target p99 < 350ms for long-seq workload) and no increase in error rate.

End of transcript.
